profile.name: Sarvesh Baskar
profile.title: AI Researcher | Multimodal AI · Reliable Agents · Reasoning & Planning

about: I am an AI researcher working on reliable multimodal agents: systems that can perceive visual environments, reason over time, and take grounded actions. My work spans vision-language models, LLM reasoning and planning, and multimodal evaluation, with a focus on visual grounding, temporal video understanding, and reducing hallucinations.

At the University of Maryland and UMBC, I have worked on VLM hallucination mitigation, trace-grounded video reasoning, executable planning from natural language, code reasoning, and persona-aware conversational agents. I also have applied engineering experience building multimodal RAG systems and agentic workflow integrations.
My long-term goal is to develop agents that combine vision, language, memory, and planning to complete reliable long-horizon tasks - first in digital environments and eventually in embodied settings.

interests.description: My technical interests center on multimodal intelligence: how models can combine language, vision, memory, and planning to make decisions that are grounded in the world rather than only fluent in text. I am especially interested in vision-language models, multimodal reasoning, planning for agents, visual grounding, hallucination mitigation, and embodied AI. A recurring theme in my work is that intelligent systems should not simply generate answers; they should know when to ask, when to look, when to verify, and when to plan. Going forward, I want to work on systems that connect VLMs, world models, and planning/control for agents that can operate across visual environments, GUIs, simulations, and robotics-inspired settings. Broadly, I am interested in AI systems that know when to look, what to remember, how to reason, when to verify, and how to act.
